dialect.detail: Appears to be Micro Focus or IBM Enterprise COBOL with function/procedure declaration extensions (DECLARE FUNCTION/PROCEDURE, SERVICE IS YFUNCOPY, INOUT/INPUT/OUTPUT parameter syntax, TYPE BOOL). The .rdz.cbl extension suggests IBM Rational Developer for z/OS (RDz) tooling, but the DECLARE FUNCTION syntax is more consistent with Micro Focus or a COBOL-2014+ extension.
evidence: INPUT x type BOOL / RETURNING y TYPE bool

purpose.domain_detail: Demonstrates and tests COBOL function/procedure declaration syntax including error cases
purpose.summary: This program is a test/demonstration of COBOL DECLARE FUNCTION and DECLARE PROCEDURE syntax. It defines multiple functions and procedures with various parameter modes (INPUT, OUTPUT, INOUT, RETURNING), intentionally including error cases (illegal FILE SECTION, mismatched parameter types, illegal GLOBAL/EXTERNAL clauses, malformed level-88 items) to exercise a compiler or static analysis tool. It appears to be a test fixture for a COBOL language tooling project.

notable_features: DECLARE FUNCTION / DECLARE PROCEDURE syntax (non-standard extension)
Intentional error cases documented in comments
No PERFORM, CALL, GOTO, or COMP-3 usage
BOM (UTF-8 BOM) at start of file
verdict.notes: The file has a UTF-8 BOM. The DECLARE FUNCTION/PROCEDURE syntax with PUBLIC/PRIVATE visibility and typed parameters is not standard COBOL but an extension. The .rdz.cbl extension suggests IBM Rational Developer for z/OS, but the syntax resembles Micro Focus OO/extended COBOL or a research/tooling dialect. The program intentionally contains error cases for testing a parser or compiler. Only DATA and PROCEDURE divisions are detected by the mechanical scanner because IDENTIFICATION DIVISION is present but the scanner may have missed it (it is present in source).
